conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: FILE-CONTROL paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: '<u>FILE-CONTROL</u>. [ file-control-entry ] ...' (cite.py --check 12.4.4.2 "file-control-entry" -> OK §12.4.4.2 General format). Grammar fileControlParagraph = FILE_CONTROL DOT fileControlClauseGroup* : required keyword, required separator period, zero-or-more file-control-entries -- exactly the format; it is optional inside inputOutputSection (FILE-CONTROL? then I-O-CONTROL?), matching §12.4.2. Probes with the pinned cobol.exe at --std 85/2002/2014/2023: (a) FILE-CONTROL. with zero entries compiles and runs (DISPLAY OK1); (b) two SELECT entries compile, write and read back both files (AAAABBBB); (c) FILE-CONTROL without its period is rejected COBOL0307 at every edition. The contents of each file-control-entry belong to §12.4.5 rows, not this one. No spec-derived golden targets the empty-paragraph form or the missing-period rejection, so test-ref is empty (test-needed). [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (no Annex E change entry for the FILE-CONTROL paragraph format)]

rows.subject: FLAG-02 directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 7.3.14.4 'If ON is explicitly or implicitly specified for an option, the warning mechanism is enabled for that option for all text that follows' OK. IsOnAt folds line-ordered events strictly before the site, per option, last toggle wins; ALL OFF (empty option list) resets every FLAG-02 option; a per-option OFF resets only that option; FLAG-14 events cannot toggle FLAG-02 options; fold spans the whole final text (to end of compilation group); PUSH/POP revocation honoured. Implicit ON (trailing ON omitted) handled by TryParse (on=true default). Probe r.cbl: ALL -> CLOSE flagged; MOVE-TO-SAME-NAME OFF -> I-O-STATUS-07 still flagged; ALL OFF -> not flagged. Also covered by unit:FlagDirectiveTests.Fold_AllOff_ResetsAPreviouslyEnabledOption. (The implicit-ALL spelling `>>FLAG-02 OFF` is rejected — recorded on FMT-7.3.14.2, not here.) || REFUTED: CONFORMS (test-ref must be empty) — The behaviour holds under every attack I made. The FLAG-02 directive inside a COPY member and statements after a multi-line COPY fold correctly, so final-text lines are consistent. A directive excluded by >>IF has no effect. Lowercase option words and a multi-option list work. ALL, then I-O-STATUS-07 OFF, then TERMINATE-WITH-VARYING ON keeps I-O-STATUS-07 off, and a later I-O-STATUS-07 ON restores it. The state persists into a second program of the same compilation group. The cited test is not usable, though: Fold_DefaultsOff_AndIsStickyForwardStrictlyAfterTheDirective builds a FLAG-14 READ-PREVIOUS event and asserts only on Flag14ReadPrevious. It pins no FLAG-02 option, so it does not close this FLAG-02 row. || editions (adjudicator): 2014 (introduced: §7.3.14.1 — incompatibilities between ISO 1989:2002 and ISO/IEC 1989:2014); 2023 (obsolete element, §7.3.14.1 NOTE); not in 1985/2002
rows.rule-text: If ON is explicitly or implicitly specified for an option, the warning mechanism is enabled for that option for all text that follows until the end of the compilation group is reached, a FLAG-02 directive is encountered that turns off all flagging options, or a FLAG-02 directive is encountered that turns off that option.

rows.subject: FLAG-02 directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 7.3.14.4 'If OFF is specified, flagging for the selected option or options is disabled' OK. OFF sets on=false for each named option (or all, for ALL OFF). Tests Compile_*_NotFlagged_WhenDirectiveOff for d/e/b; probe r.cbl line 20 (after ALL OFF) not flagged. || REFUTED: CONFORMS (test-ref must be empty) — The behaviour conforms: OFF disables a previously enabled option, whether per option or via ALL OFF (probe). The cited test Compile_MoveToSameName_NotFlagged_WhenDirectiveOff has ONLY `>>FLAG-02 MOVE-TO-SAME-NAME OFF` and nothing enabled before it. It passes identically under the GR5 default-off even if OFF were a no-op, so it cannot distinguish GR3 from GR5 and does not pin GR3's branch (disabling an enabled option). || editions (adjudicator): 2014 (introduced: §7.3.14.1 — incompatibilities between ISO 1989:2002 and ISO/IEC 1989:2014); 2023 (obsolete element, §7.3.14.1 NOTE); not in 1985/2002
rows.rule-text: If OFF is specified, flagging for the selected option or options is disabled.

rows.subject: FLAG-02 directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 7.3.14.4 'If the FLAG-02 directive is not specified, the default for all options is off' OK. IsOnAt starts on=false; Run returns without walking when no event exists. Also unit:FlagDirectiveTests.Fold_DefaultsOff_AndIsStickyForwardStrictlyAfterTheDirective. || REFUTED: CONFORMS (test-ref must be empty) — The behaviour conforms: IsOnAt starts on=false, Run returns without a walk when no events exist, and a CLOSE WITH NO REWIND before any FLAG-02 directive is not flagged (p1 line 14, p2 line 13). The cited test Compile_NoDirective_EmitsNoFlagWarning compiles the FLAG-14 ReadPreviousProgram and asserts only the absence of COBOLNET1621, the FLAG-14 code. It contains no FLAG-02-flaggable construct and never checks COBOLNET1620, so it does not pin the FLAG-02 default. || editions (adjudicator): 2014 (introduced: §7.3.14.1 — incompatibilities between ISO 1989:2002 and ISO/IEC 1989:2014); 2023 (obsolete element, §7.3.14.1 NOTE); not in 1985/2002
rows.rule-text: If the FLAG-02 directive is not specified, the default for all options is off.

rows.subject: FREE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: Format `FREE { data-name-1 } ...` (cite.py --check 14.9.15.2 "FREE" -> OK). Grammar `freeStatement : FREE dataReference+` = one-or-more operands; dataReference also admits qualification/subscripting, which only reaches a data-pointer inside a STRONG typedef (13.18.60.3 SR14 --check OK confines USAGE POINTER to level 1 or STRONG-typedef subordinates) - the pointer then has to be referenced that way, so this is not a leniency beyond reference-format rules. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, probe/free): f1 `FREE P Q N P` parses and runs; f3 --std 85 -> COBOLNET0900 'FREE requires COBOL-2002'; --std 2002 compiles and runs. Existing goldens conformance:2002/pointer_alloc and allocate_initialized exercise only single-operand FREE, so no spec-derived test covers the repeated-operand shape -> test-ref empty. [code-location note: edition gate] || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (FREE is absent from ISO 1989:1985; the 2023 Annex E records only 2014->2023 changes, and 14.9.15 is unchanged text in 2014/2023)

rows.subject: FREE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR1 a) release + set NULL when the pointer identifies the START of currently ALLOCATEd storage; b) NULL -> no action; c) otherwise EC-STORAGE-NOT-ALLOC (cite.py --check 14.9.15.4 a) and c) -> OK; Table EC-STORAGE-NOT-ALLOC is NF). CobolPtr.Free: null/IsNull -> Null (b); CellPointer{Offset:0, Cell{Allocated:true,Freed:false}} -> mark Freed, clear image+slots, return Null (a; 'contents become undefined' realized as a loud deref); else notAlloc=true, operand unchanged (c). EmitFree raises EC-STORAGE-NOT-ALLOC nonfatal only when checking is enabled (14.6.13.1.4 - unchecked nonfatal continues). Probes f1 (>>TURN EC-STORAGE-NOT-ALLOC CHECKING ON + USE declarative): FREE of NULL N -> no EC; FREE of R = P UP BY 1 (not start) -> EC, R unchanged; FREE P Q (Q an alias of already-freed P) -> P NULL, Q gets EC (no longer 'currently allocated'); FREE of SET P TO ADDRESS OF W (WORKING-STORAGE, not ALLOCATEd) -> EC, P unchanged; f3 checking off -> no EC, EXCEPTION-STATUS blank. All three arms verified. Only arm a) has a golden (conformance:2002/pointer_alloc, FREED=YES); arms b)/c) have none -> test-ref empty. || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (FREE is absent from ISO 1989:1985; the 2023 Annex E records only 2014->2023 changes, and 14.9.15 is unchanged text in 2014/2023)
rows.rule-text: The FREE statement is processed as follows: a) If the data-pointer referenced by data-name-1 identifies the start of storage that is currently allocated by an ALLOCATE statement, that storage is released and the data-pointer referenced by data-name-1 is set to NULL, the length of the released storage is the length of the storage obtained by the ALLOCATE statement, and the contents of any data items located within the released storage area become undefined; b) otherwise, if the data-pointer referenced by data-name-1 contains the predefined address NULL, no action is taken for that operand; c) otherwise, the EC-STORAGE-NOT-ALLOC exception condition is set to exist.

rows.subject: FREE statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR2: per-operand implicit FREE in source order; nonfatal -> resume at the next implicit FREE; fatal not terminating -> resume at the next implicit FREE (cite.py --check 14.9.15.4 "processing resumes at the next implicit FREE statement, if any" -> OK 2)). BindFree builds BoundImplicitSeries.Of(one BoundFree per data-name-1). Probes: f1 `FREE P Q N P` -> P freed first then Q (alias) raises EC, N no-op, final P no-op (order observed); f2-equivalent f3 `FREE Q P2` with Q not-start: nonfatal EC and P2 still freed (resumption after nonfatal, both checked and unchecked); f6 fatal arm: STRONG-typedef pointer table `FREE PX OF V(I) P2` with I out of range, EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT checked, declarative completing normally -> abnormal termination, which is 14.6.13.1.3 item 5 (--check OK), correct; f7 same with RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT in the declarative -> 'P2 NULL' then 'AFTER', i.e. processing resumed at the next implicit FREE. All halves verified; no golden exercises a multi-operand FREE -> test-ref empty. [code-location note: (BoundImplicitSeries of one BoundFree per operand)] || editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (FREE is absent from ISO 1989:1985; the 2023 Annex E records only 2014->2023 changes, and 14.9.15 is unchanged text in 2014/2023)
rows.rule-text: If more than one data-name-1 is specified in a FREE statement, the result of executing this FREE statement is the same as if a separate FREE statement had been written for each data-name-1 in the same order as specified in the FREE statement. If an implicit FREE statement results in an exception condition being raised and the exception condition is nonfatal, after any applicable exception processing statements are executed, processing resumes at the next implicit FREE statement, if any. If the exception condition is fatal and the applicable exception processing statements do not result in abnormal run unit termination, processing resumes at the next implicit FREE statement, if applicable. If there is no next implicit FREE statement, processing resumes at the next executable statement as if no exception condition was raised during the execution of the FREE statement.

rows.subject: FUNCTION-ID paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: §11.5.2 prints Format 1 `FUNCTION-ID. user-function-name-1 [ AS literal-1 ] .` and Format 2 `FUNCTION-ID. function-prototype-name-1 [ AS literal-1 ] IS PROTOTYPE.` (IS not underlined => optional; FUNCTION-ID, AS, PROTOTYPE underlined; both periods required). cite.py --check 11.5.2 "Format 1 (definition)" OK; --check 11.5.2 "Format 2 (prototype)" OK. Grammar: `FUNCTION_ID DOT programName externalizedNamePhrase? prototypePhrase? DOT`, prototypePhrase = `IS? PROTOTYPE`, externalizedNamePhrase = `AS literal` (narrowed by ExternalizedName.Screen, the §11.5.3 SR1 row owned by landed PB303). Probes with the pinned cobol.exe (out/probe/fid): p1 Format 2 with AS + IS (`FUNCTION-ID. FIDPA AS "FIDREAL" IS PROTOTYPE.`) compiles+runs at 2002 and 2023 (P=000049); p2 Format 2 with IS omitted (`FUNCTION-ID. FIDPB PROTOTYPE.`) compiles+runs at 2002/2023; p4 missing period after FUNCTION-ID rejected (COBOL0307); p5 reversed order `IS PROTOTYPE AS "X"` rejected (COBOLNET0901 on AS — rejection correct, message names reservation rather than position); --std 85 rejects the prototype tail, the AS phrase and function reference with COBOLNET0900 (edition gate). Format 1 with/without AS is exercised by conformance:2002/pb303_as_externalized_name and conformance:2002/udf_invocation; Format 2 without AS by conformance:2002/udf_prototype; NO existing golden covers Format 2 WITH AS literal-1 or the IS-omitted spelling, so test-ref is left empty (test-needed for those arms) rather than claiming whole-format coverage. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2002, 2014, 2023 (FUNCTION-ID / user-defined functions and function prototypes are COBOL-2002 introductions; the 2023 Annex E lists no change to §11.5). Not in COBOL-85.
rows.rule-text:
Format 1 (definition): 
 FUNCTION-ID. user-function-name-1 [ AS literal-1 ] .
Format 2 (prototype): 
 FUNCTION-ID. function-prototype-name-1 [ AS literal-1 ] IS PROTOTYPE.

rows.adjudicator-notes: VOLUNTARY row: A.1 69 is optional and need not be documented. §14.6.13.1.3 8) (cite.py OK). All 17 Warning descriptors in DiagnosticCatalog were scanned; only COBOLNET1662 (order-table-unresolved) anticipates a fatal EC (EC-ORDER-NOT-SUPPORTED, L3 Fatal in ExceptionCatalog). Probes /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s3/probe: f69.cob (>>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING ON; S(4:5), E(6) with OCCURS 5, 10 / 0) compiles clean and ends at run time with EC-BOUND-REF-MOD (fatal), exit 1; f69off.cob runs START/END, exit 0; o69.cob (ORDER TABLE OT IS "BOGUS-TABLE") -> compile warning COBOLNET1662 and a run; o69on.cob with checking -> EC-ORDER-NOT-SUPPORTED (fatal) at run time. The adjudication refuter's sweep (SQRT(-1), LOG(0), NUMVAL("ABC") etc.) agrees. No spec-derived test pins the item. Owning note kb/Work/PB1535 (no item-specific note).

rows.subject: Figurative constant values
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'The space format represents one or more of the character space in the computer's runtime coded character set.' (cite.py --check 8.3.3.6.4 -> OK 5)). FillChar 'S' -> ' ' for alphanumeric and national; probe probe/figurative-constant-values/p1.cob MOVE SPACE TO PIC X(3), PIC N(3) -> '[   |   ]'; p6.cob INSPECT TALLYING FOR ALL SPACE counts 3 blanks. The boolean arm ('S' against a boolean operand -> '0') is DETERMINATION D-B2 (CONFORMANCE.md), reachable only via §14.9.25.4 GR2's zero-length-literal substitution since MOVE SR7 forbids a written SPACE to a boolean item — a documented latitude choice, not a divergence. No spec-derived test isolates the space character itself; test-needed.
rows.rule-text: The space format represents one or more of the character space in the computer's runtime coded character set.

rows.subject: Figurative constant values
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'The quote format represents one or more of the quotation mark character ' " ' in the computer's runtime coded character set. The word QUOTE or QUOTES shall not be used in place of a quotation symbol to bound a literal.' (cite.py --check 8.3.3.6.4 -> OK 8)). First half: FillChar 'Q' -> '"' (both classes); probe probe/figurative-constant-values/p1.cob MOVE QUOTE TO PIC X(3)/PIC N(3) -> '"""|"""', DISPLAY QUOTE -> '"'. Second half: the lexer recognizes literal delimiters only as quotation symbols (§8.3.5 SR5); QUOTE is a figurative token (KindOf) with no delimiter role anywhere in the grammar, so it cannot bound a literal. No spec-derived test isolates the quote character; test-needed.
rows.rule-text: The quote format represents one or more of the quotation mark character ' " ' in the computer's runtime coded character set. The word QUOTE or QUOTES shall not be used in place of a quotation symbol to bound a literal.

rows.subject: Figurative constant values (representation of zero, space, and quote)
rows.adjudicator-notes: Row states the representation of ZERO/SPACE/QUOTE (§8.3.3.6.4 1), cite.py OK). Probe /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s3/probe/p74.cob at --std 2014 and 2023: ORD of SPACE/ZERO/QUOTE in PIC X = 33/49/35, in PIC N = 33/49/35; SPACE=X"20", QUOTE=X"22", ZERO=X"30", national QUOTE = NX"0022" all true. At --std 85 the alphanumeric half holds and national data is gated (COBOLNET0900). FigurativeConstants.FillChar: 'Z'->'0', 'S'->' ', 'Q'->'"'. No spec-derived test pins the code values, so test-ref is empty. Row closes the documentation gap owned by kb/Work/PB1397 (item 74).
